messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT PAGE — SLO alert: streaming /v1/chat/stream p99 spike (SLO breach) detected 03:12 UTC. Auto-paging oncall.

alice: seeing it, got the page. oncall for infra today. jumping in.

ben: confirmed in telemetry — sudden p99 jump aligned with a quant calibration rollout at 03:10 UTC to gpt2-quant-int8-v3.

carla: gist of numbers:
```
p95: 210ms (baseline 120ms)
p99: 1.12s (baseline 320ms)
streaming stall rate: 0.8% -> baseline 0.02%
error rate: 0.1% (auth/timeouts mostly stream stalls)
affected routes: /v1/chat/stream for model=redwood/gpt2-quant-int8-v3
percent traffic hitting cal profile: ~42% global
```

dave: thanks. I'm taking lead for live mitigation and ops bridge. creating bridge now — ops-bridge invite sent.

ops-bridge: Bridge created: https://redwood/bridge/INC-1749998888 — dial-in pinned.

erin: support: customer pages starting to roll in, small spike of user complaints for streaming timeouts (~5 customers currently). Not seeing major data leakage.

alice: immediate mitigation plan: 1) stop further rollout of int8 calibration 2) route traffic off the calibrated profile to fallback fp32/qtz-safe variant 3) scale up dedicated streaming pool in EU to reduce queueing 4) enable conservative KV prefix caching for streaming.

ben: I can run rollback now. proposed command:
```
# revert calibration profile for gpt2-quant-int8-v3
/redwood rollback-profile --model gpt2-quant-int8-v3 --to-tag v3-2026-03-14 --force
```

carla: adding a quick routing rule to bypass the profile for streaming routes until we have a fix. Patch pinned for 15m then reassess.

dave: executing steps 1+2 now. ben + alice coordinate rollback and route change. carla watch autoscaler. erin monitor CS queue and notify any high-impact customers asap.

ben: rollback started at 03:18 UTC. logs: 
```
[03:18:05] rollback job queued
[03:18:22] profile traffic drain started (40% -> 0% target)
[03:19:10] route policy updated: streaming -> model_variant=fp32-safe
[03:19:40] rollback confirmed on 8/12 regions
```

alice: enabling conservative KV caching and disabling dynamic batching for streaming in the hot path — trade latency for stability.

carla: autoscaler spiked but responding. spun up +30% streaming pods in eu-west-1 and na-central.

ops-bridge: realtime metrics show p99 trending down. current numbers: p95=145ms p99=380ms stream stall rate=0.05% (03:25 UTC).

erin: CS update: notified top 10 customers impacted by timeouts, offered temporary retry guidance. no SLA credits asked yet.

dave: good. holding oncall for 45m to watch for re-emergence. going to escalate to research + inference tuning if we see tail reappear after rollback.

ben: quick note — telemetry indicates the calibration changed kernel selection causing intermittent KV-dequant contention under streaming long contexts. repro rate low in offline tests but high in production due to mixed batch sizes.

alice: filing follow-up action items:
- postmortem assigned to ben (inference) + carla (sre) due EOD tomorrow
- add regression test for long-context streaming under new quant kernels
- update calibration rollout playbook: staged canary size, perf guardrails (p99 cutoffs), automatic rollback on tail breach
- contact perf/research about safer fallback heuristics (fp8->int8 fallthrough)

carla: creating an incident label and schedule standup at 03:40 UTC to review telemetry and rollout logs.

ops-bridge: status update at 03:31 UTC — mitigation in place, p99 reduced under alert threshold, customer impact limited to transient timeouts. Continue monitoring for 60m.

erin: logging all CS contacts and ticket IDs in the incident doc. sending templated update to affected customers now.

dave: marking priority P1 -> sustained monitoring. if p99 > 500ms or stall rate > 0.2% we re-open full page.

alice: short-term closure: mitigation successful; scheduled rollback completed across all regions by 03:22 UTC. moving to handoff. oncall dave -> alice for 1h watch.

dave: handing off to alice. I'll remain on the bridge for 15 more minutes then drop.

alice: taking watch. follow-ups: coordinate postmortem, update runbooks, block further auto-calib rollouts until the new tests are in.

ben: putting a draft of the perf investigation in the incident doc now (includes kernel traces and sample request traces).

carla: assigning incident label: quant-calib-tail-1749998888.

ops-bridge: Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. Final notes: suspected root cause = quant calibration kernel selection leading to intermittent dequant/KV contention under streaming long contexts; primary mitigation = rollback + routing fallback + scaling + KV caching; follow-ups = testing + playbook updates + perf/regression checks.

erin: closing note — CS will issue a customer update once the postmortem is ready.

alice: thumbs. good job everyone. :thumbsup: :coffee:

incident-bot: Incident closed for paging at 03:40 UTC — monitoring window open for 60m.
